question.problem:
Find the value of the constant $c$ that makes the function $h(x)$ below continuous at $x=2.$

$$
h(x)=\{\begin{aligned}{3}^{cx}\,\,, & x\le 2 \\ {x}^{5}-5, & x>2\end{aligned}
$$
question.worked_solution:
At $x=2,$ the left-sided limit is

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to {2}^{-}}h(x) & =h(2) \\  & ={3}^{c(2)} \\  & ={3}^{2c},\end{aligned}
$$

 

and the right-sided limit is

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to {2}^{+}}h(x) & ={lim}_{x\to {2}^{+}}({x}^{5}-5) \\  & ={2}^{5}-5 \\  & =27.\end{aligned}
$$

In order for $h(x)$ to be continuous at $x=2,$ we require that

$$
\begin{aligned}{3}^{2c} & =27 \\ {3}^{2c} & ={3}^{3} \\ 2c & =3 \\ c & =\frac{3}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $h(x)$ is continuous at $x=2$ for $c=\frac{3}{2}.$
